episodes.177485: Following the passage of the upper trough which moved across the area on March 29. A cold an unstable airmass prevailed over central California on March 30. As a result, showers and a few thunderstorms developed over the San Joaquin Valley resulting in localized flooding as well as at least one funnel cloud report.
episodes.178224: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 30th. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.178631: The combination of tropical moisture and a slow moving cold front allowed for scattered showers and thunderstorms across southern Florida throughout the day. Heavier showers arrived late in the afternoon and evening, bringing rain to areas across Miami-Dade County.
episodes.178632: A weak front moving through South Florida triggered a few showers over the Atlantic waters offshore of Southeast Florida.
episodes.178651: A weak atmospheric river produced widespread moderate rainfall and high-elevation snow across Southern California March 29-30. Several stronger thunderstorm cells occurred across San Diego County, resulting in a Severe Thunderstorm Warning and a Tornado Warning. No damage was reported with these warnings.
episodes.178984: Cold low pressure digging south from the Gulf of Alaska brought isolated high winds to the Spring Mountains and a few thunderstorms to the Mojave Desert.
episodes.179199: A deep upper level low brought wraparound precipitation to the region. Warmer surface temperatures allowed for heavy rainfall with resulting ponding on major roads and intersections in the Snake River Valley, while heavy snow accumulated in elevations above 5000 feet.
episodes.179420: High pressure ridging over the eastern United States provided an environment conducive for waterspout formation, with converging northeast to east winds over the Lower Florida Keys.  Convective cloud lines in the western lee of the Lower Florida Keys produced two rounds of waterspout formation during the afternoon hours.

events.narrative: The mesonet station WWA01 10.7 miles southeast of Horseshoe Bend measured 1.56 inches of rain.
The mesonet station BOII 1.7 miles southeast of Boise measured 1.15 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station TT289 at Crestline Trail in the Boise foothills measured 1.08 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station at BSUI1 measured 1.32 inches of heavy rain.
The mesonet station GW0891 in Boise measured 1.09 inches of rain.
The mesonet station LLAI1 at the Boise Weather Forecast Office RAWS measured 1.13 inches of rain.
The mesonet station 1452D 2 miles east of Boise measured 1.10 inches of rain.

A post on social media showed notable street flooding in Miami. The roadway near the intersection of Biscayne Boulevard and NE 15th Street had an estimated five inches of water across the road. Rainfall measurements in the general area were in the two to three inch range.
California Highway Patrol reported the County Line Rd. was completely flooded between Rd. 192 and Rd. 200.

events.county: Deerfield Beach To Ocean Reef Fl
events.narrative: A video from social media showed a waterspout off the coast of Fisher Island.
The Department of Highways reported roadway flooding at SR-74W and College Grove Avenue, with 0.45-0.55 inch of rain reported in the previous 24 hours.

events.county: Gulf Of Mexico From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To 5 Fathoms
events.narrative: A family of waterspouts was observed in association with a convective cloud line over the Gulfside waters adjacent to the Lower Florida Keys from the Saddlebunch Keys to Key West.  Numerous reports and photographs were submitted by NWS employees and the public.  Each waterspout lasted about 5 to 15 minutes before dissipation. Nearly 20 waterspouts were observed.
Report posted on Facebook of a funnel cloud in Arvin.
